name: Intestinal Lymphangiectasia

prevalence.estimate: Unknown; fewer than 500 cases reported in literature

criteria.description: Dilated lymphatics on intestinal biopsy (endoscopic or surgical)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Protein-losing enteropathy demonstrated by low albumin/protein plus elevated fecal alpha-1-antitrypsin, combined with histological evidence of dilated intestinal lymphatics.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Primary form (Waldmann disease) is congenital. Secondary forms result from conditions causing lymphatic obstruction (constrictive pericarditis, lymphoma, Fontan procedure, SLE, sarcoidosis).

pathognomonic.notes: Often asymmetric; may present as lymphedema

rare.notes: Increased risk of B-cell lymphoma reported
Due to calcium and vitamin D malabsorption

imaging: CT enterography: thickened small bowel folds, particularly jejunum
Tc-99m albumin scintigraphy: demonstrates enteric protein loss
genetic: Primary form may be associated with chromosomal abnormalities (Turner syndrome, Noonan syndrome)
VEGFR3 pathway dysregulation implicated in some cases
other: Upper endoscopy: 'snowflake' appearance of duodenal/jejunal mucosa (white-tipped villi)
Capsule endoscopy: diffuse white spots on small bowel mucosa
Small bowel biopsy: dilated lacteals in villous tips (pathognomonic histology)

distinguishingFeatures: Constrictive pericarditis causes secondary lymphangiectasia from elevated venous pressure
Jugular venous distension and Kussmaul sign present
Celiac has villous atrophy, not dilated lacteals
Positive celiac serologies in celiac disease
Nephrotic syndrome does not have elevated fecal alpha-1-antitrypsin

redFlags: Severe edema with respiratory compromise (pleural effusion, ascites)
Recurrent serious infections suggesting severe immunodeficiency
Development of lymphoma (watch for new lymphadenopathy, B-symptoms)
Tetany or seizures from severe hypocalcemia
references: Vignes S, Bellanger J. Primary intestinal lymphangiectasia (Waldmann's disease). Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2008;3:5.
Wen J, et al. Primary intestinal lymphangiectasia: four case reports and a review of the literature. Dig Dis Sci. 2010;55(12):3466-3472.
Waldmann TA, et al. The role of the gastrointestinal system in idiopathic hypoproteinemia. Gastroenterology. 1961;41:197-207.
